prompt:
Create a production pixel sprite sheet of 4 composable battle effect layers, each exactly THREE animation frames. Image input is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match crisp white/steel pixel clusters but draw entirely new four rows. Transparent RGBA background. Layout precisely 3 equal columns by 4 equal rows with generous empty gutters; twelve sprites total. Each row represents one effect onset, peak, dispersal. All three frames share same center, no per-frame rescaling. Flat screen-facing early handheld RPG battle VFX, NOT side-scrolling weapon art, no scenery or characters, no ground plane, no perspective tilt, no labels, no text, no gray checkerboard. Limited white, pearl and cool steel gray palette, no blue colored glow. Preserve large transparent centers and simple chunky pixels. Shapes readable at 48px.
Row 1: CASTER SPELL CIRCLE. An upright front-on magic rune circle centered around an empty space for caster. First frame sparse ring arcs and four small rune ticks; second complete delicate double ring with simple angular rune marks, large empty center; third ring breaks into fading small arcs. This circle is a separate overlay under the caster sprite before recipient impact, not a solid disc or ground ellipse.
Row 2: BLOCK. Stylized front-on shield outline with very large hollow transparent center, brief compact contact sparks at its upper right edge. First shield outline appears, second shield holds and angular contact spark appears, third shield fragments into a few fading edges. Keep visually distinct from the upright oval ward bubble.
Row 3: EVADE. Three short narrow offset curved motion traces surrounding an EMPTY central gap; sparse near-vertical slip marks, no shield, no slash across the center. First trace, second staggered traces displaced sideways, third traces dissipate into tiny dashes. This overlays a dodging actor without depicting a person.
Row 4: RETREAT. Two broad separated backward-pointing chevrons and short receding horizontal speed dashes, oriented left; first one hollow chevron, second two offset hollow chevrons, third sparse trailing dashes. This is a tactical withdrawal motion cue over an actor, not damage. Clearly different from evade's slim curved traces.
Each effect is an independent transparent sprite layer to combine with existing character and elemental layers. No arrows in any row except the retreat chevrons. No other effects. Exactly four rows and three columns.
